name: Volcanic Sorrel
description: Oxalis vulcanicola, commonly known as Volcanic Sorrel or Molten Lava, is a tender spreading perennial native to volcanic regions of Central America. It belongs to the Oxalidaceae family and features semi-succulent stems with trifoliate (three-part) leaves that are pinkish-orange in spring, greener in summer, and deep magenta in autumn, with reddish stems. The plant grows 20-25 cm tall and spreads 60 cm or more, forming a low mounding mat. It produces small five-petaled yellow flowers (1-2.5 cm) with delicate red lines in the throat from spring to autumn. It prefers bright light and well-drained, sandy or humus-rich soil. Suitable for terrariums, hanging baskets, and as a houseplant.
careTips: Bright direct or indirect light for best foliage color; partial shade tolerated but less vibrant
Water when top 2-3 inches of soil is dry; tolerates occasional dry spells
Well-drained substrate essential; equal parts loam, leaf mould, and grit works well
Feed 1-2 times during growing season with half-strength balanced fertilizer
Contains soluble oxalates - toxic if ingested in large quantities by humans and pets
